Tempo

/TEM-poh/ — rhymes with memo · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Tempo is the speed or pace at which something, especially a piece of music, moves.

The drummer sets the tempo, and the whole band follows.

Worked Example

The conductor raises her baton, and the entire orchestra shifts from a slow, mournful opening to a bright, rapid allegro—every instrument locked in to the new tempo she has set.

Tempo is more precise than "speed" or "pace" because it names the *intentional, coordinated* rate that a leader establishes for a group. In this musical context, tempo captures not just how fast the music moves, but that all the musicians move together at that exact rate.

How Tempo Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

pace

pace: the rate at which something moves forward

speed

speed: simply how fast something travels or happens

rhythm

rhythm: a repeating pattern of beats or movement

Antonyms

stillness

stillness: the complete absence of motion or sound

standstill

standstill: a full stop in which nothing moves

How Strong Is It? — stillness → shuffle → tempo → frenzy

stillness vs. tempo

stillness vs. tempo: Stillness sits at the very bottom of the scale, far below tempo: stillness is the complete absence of movement, while a tempo is a steady, measurable pace that carries the music forward.

shuffle vs. tempo

shuffle vs. tempo: A shuffle is slower and looser than a tempo — a shuffle drags along irregularly, while a tempo keeps deliberate, controlled time.

frenzy vs. tempo

frenzy vs. tempo: A frenzy is far more intense than a tempo: a tempo is speed under control, but a frenzy is wild, racing movement that has broken free of any steady beat.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tempo

Root — tempo: time (Latin tempus, 'time, season, portion of time') (Italian, from Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Tempo is simply the Italian word for 'time,' inherited from Latin tempus. It names how time is being measured out — the speed or pace at which music, or anything else, moves.

Use the root in a new word: temporary

Use the root in a new word: temporary: A temporary job lasts only a short time — the same Latin root tempus, meaning 'time,' that gives music its tempo.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / musical

Use tempo when describing the controlled rate of music or a coordinated, intentional pace in a structured setting like a rehearsal. For everyday motion or speed without coordination, pace or speed is better.
